title: Electrical Servicing
description:
Rushmoor Borough Council - the 'council' - is inviting expressions of interest from suitably qualified and experienced suppliers for a three (3) year + two (2) year contract for the provision of electrical servicing for a range of council buildings (29 in total), including the civic offices, crematorium, sports pavilions, community centres and offices.\r
\r
The Council recognises and accepts its responsibility as a building owner and the duty of care placed on it by legislation and takes all reasonably practicable steps to ensure that the buildings under its direct control are managed and operated safely.  \r
\r
This contractor is to assist the Council in complying with its duties under the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 to include: \r
â€¢	Electrical Installation Condition Report servicing to be carried out every five years\r
â€¢	Portable Appliance Testing to be carried out every two years\r
â€¢	Reactive Works\r
\r
The Contract is anticipated to commence on Monday 23rd October 2023 for Rushmoor Borough Council.\r
\r
The value of the contract requirement equates to approximately £75,000. \r
\r
The council is undertaking the procurement process in general accordance with the open procedure. It should be noted that the contract value falls below the statutory threshold for services set out within Public Contracts Regulations (2015) and as such only the aspects of the regulations concerned with below threshold contracts shall apply. The council will undertake a procurement process to award the contract in line with the summary programme set out below:\r
\r
â€¢ ITT published on SEBP & project published on Contracts Finder - Friday 28th July\r
â€¢ Deadline for requests for clarification - Friday 18th August 2023, 23:59\r
â€¢ Tender return deadline - Friday 8th September 2023, 16:00\r
â€¢ Contract award - Monday 2nd October 2023\r
â€¢ Target contract execution - Monday 23rd October 2023\r
\r
The Council is utilising an electronic tendering tool to manage this procurement and communicate with Tenderers. Accordingly, there will be no hard copy documents issued to Tenderers and all communications with the Council, including the submission of Tenderers' Responses, will be conducted via the ProContract system, which can be accessed using the following link: https://procontract.due-north.com/Login\r
\r
Suppliers not currently registered on the ProContract procurement portal can complete a simple registration process by clicking the following link and registering https://procontract.due-north.com/Register

title: TENDER FOR THE SUPPLY AND/OR SUPPLY, INSTALLATION & MAINTENANCE OF SIGNAGE ACROSS HAMPSHIRE UNDER A FRAMEWORK AGREEMENT
description:
Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council (the council) are seeking to commission competent and experienced contractor(s) for the provision of signage at various site locations throughout Hampshire. The Council is acting as Lead Authority on behalf of the authorities listed below:  \r
â€¢	Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council\r
â€¢	East Hampshire District Council\r
â€¢	Eastleigh Borough Council\r
â€¢	Fareham Borough Council\r
â€¢	Gosport Borough Council\r
â€¢	Hampshire County Council\r
â€¢	Hart District Council\r
â€¢	Havant Borough Council\r
â€¢	Isle of Wight Council\r
â€¢	New Forest Borough Council\r
â€¢	Portsmouth City Council\r
â€¢	Rushmoor Borough Council\r
â€¢	Southampton City Council\r
â€¢	Test Valley Borough Council\r
â€¢	Winchester City Council\r
\r
Other authorities that are part of this process comprise:\r
\r
â€¢	Town and Parish Councils within Hampshire\r
â€¢	Junior, Primary and Secondary Schools in the Hampshire County Council local authority area, (private schools are not included in the Framework).\r
\r
The main objective of this invitation to Tender(ITT) is to establish a Framework Contract, potentially with multiple suppliers (however, only 1 supplier will be awarded to each of the four lots which could potentially be the same supplier) to cover the needs of each organisation that uses the framework.\r
\r
The framework will  cover the supply of various types of signage, ranging from very small quantities (one item) to larger orders.  As requirements differ for each organisation, the contract will comprise of 'supply only' and/or 'supply and installation' Lots.  \r
\r
The framework will be split into four Lots as detailed below:\r
\r
Lot 1 	Street Name Plates	Supply Only\r
Lot 2	Street Name Plates	Supply and Installation/maintenance\r
Lot 3	Road Signage (including Directional Signs, Information signs)	Supply Only\r
Lot 4 	Road Signage (including Directional Signs, Information signs)	Supply and Installation/maintenance\r
\r
The Councils intents to award only one supplier to each Lot, however, tenderers can bid for one or more Lots; though each Lot will be evaluated separately and response documents must be provided for each lot that the tenderer is responding to. Therefore, the potential successful tenderer could be appointed to more than one lot.\r

title: Stray Dog Collection, Kennelling and Rehoming Service
description:
Rushmoor Borough Council ('the Council') is inviting tenders from suitably qualified suppliers to provide services for the collections, kennelling and re-homing of stray dogs. Since 2008, local authorities have had sole responsibility for discharging responsibilities for stray dogs. Sections 149 and 150 of the Environmental Protection Act 1990 and the Environmental Protection (Stray Dogs) Regulations 1992 set out the provisions and duties of local authorities for seizing and dealing with stray dogs. The council also has legal obligations under the Microchipping of Dogs Regulations 2015 and the Animal Welfare Act 2006. The Council is currently looking to undertake outsourcing 'Stray Dog' service to include collection, kennelling and rehoming of stray dogs. 	

The Council is utilising an electronic tendering tool to manage this procurement and communicate with Tenderers.  Accordingly, there will be no hard copy documents issued to Tenderers and all communications with the Council, including the submission of Tenderers' Responses, will be conducted via the ProContract system, which can be accessed using the following link: https://procontract.due-north.com/Supplier/Advert/View?advertId=d6d3c422-cc09-ed11-8116-005056b64545&fromProjectDashboard=False&fromRfxSummary=False&selectWorkgroup=False&fromAdvertEvent=False&fromActivityDashboard=False

title: Asbestos Testing and Consultancy - Multi Contractor Framework - AWARD
description:
Portsmouth City Council 'the council' is inviting tenders from suitably qualified and experienced suppliers for inclusion on a multi-supplier framework agreement for the provision of asbestos surveying and consultancy services. 
      
      The framework will be used to source asbestos testing and consultancy services for the council's portfolio of 15,000 social housing properties and 900 corporate assets. The framework will also be accessible to Gosport Borough Council, Rushmoor Borough Council and Southampton City Council, however the council can provide no guarantees in respect of usage by these additional named Contracting Authorities.
      
      The council is targeting to have awarded the framework agreement by 13th November 2023 with commencement from 8th January 2024. Once established the framework agreement will run for a term of 4 years.
      
      Spend per annum via the framework agreement is estimated to be in the region of £450 - £500K. Call off contracts may be let which have terms which go beyond the framework term as long as they are awarded within the 4 year term of the framework.  
      
      The highest scoring 5 suppliers will be appointed onto the framework agreement on a ranked basis. 
      
      Concurrently with establishing the framework, a term service contract for standard services incorporating a schedule of rates will be awarded to the highest scoring supplier on the framework. The term service agreement will be used for services to sites which are of a consistent value, quantity and complexity and fall within agreed Schedule of Rates. The term service contract will run for 4 years with an option to extend in increments to be agreed for a further 2 years. 
      
      Services procured through the term service contract is estimated at approximately £350,000 per annum. Individual orders are likely to be frequent with value varying between £250 - £5,000, however generally they will be in the lower value range. The 
      contract will be let using the council's bespoke term service contract. 
      
      Contractors allocated onto the framework will provide contingency for the term service contact on a ranked basis in case of any capacity or significant performance issues.
      
      In addition to the Term Service contract all contractors allocated onto the framework will be invited to participate in mini competitions for non-standard services.  Non standard services will be characterised by  being of a higher value in comparison to one off dwelling surveys, volume, complexity or do not fall within the agreed schedule of rates .
      
      Estimated value for non-standard services is approximately £150,000 per annum, approximately £100,000 of this demand is estimated to be from the council  and £50,000 of demand from other named contracting authorities, The number of call offs are likely to be low across the framework term, with value expected to vary with no upper or lower limit, however generally will  be between £5,000 - £50,000. title: Dental Electronic Referral System (DERS) across the South East
description:
The Commissioners wished to seek a single provider to deliver DERS across the South East. The Crown Commercial Services (CCS) Framework RM6259 Vertical Application Solutions - Lot 2 'Education, Community Health and Social Care Solutions' was used to run a "further competition". A total of thirty-two providers are approved on the CCS framework agreement for Lot 2 and were contacted prior to the further competition ITT being published.

DERS is an end-to-end digital software system which is cloud-based. The service enables the patient journey from General Dental Services into specialist services and forms an essential part of the NHS dental system. DERS will ensure that referrals made by dentists, continue to be monitored and evaluated in line with Guidelines specifically, to:
•	Provide clinicians with a single mechanism to refer patients that require specialist and specialised NHS dental services.
•	Improve the quality of referrals in order to support effective triage.
•	Enable patients to access care that is most suited to their needs.
•	Improve the efficiency of the referral process.
•	Provide accurate referral information to support clinical service evaluation and development.
•	Achieve value for money.

Geography covered:
Hampshire & Isle of Wight
Frimley (Rushmoor, Hart, Bracknell Forest, Slough, Windsor and Maidenhead)
Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire and Berkshire West
Dorset

Contract start date: 01/02/2025
Contract award date: 10/03/2025
Contract term: 2 years with an extension option for any period up to a further 2 years
Contract value (initial 2 year term): £1,374,400
Contract value (inclusive of 2 x extension years): £2,748,800

Following notification of the outcome of the procurement, the contracting authority observed a voluntary 10 day standstill period prior to awarding the contract.

This procurement has been carried out by NHS South, Central and West Commissioning Support Unit (SCW) on behalf of the Commissioners.

title: Contract for the Supply, Installation and Maintenance of Bus Shelters and Information Panels, including right to Display Advertising on Bus Shelters  - AWARD
description:
Hampshire County Council invites applications from suitably experienced organisations who wish to be considered for selection to tender for the Supply, Installation and Maintenance of Bus Shelters and Information Panels, including right to Display Advertising on Bus Shelters.
      
      The Authority is seeking a concessionaire to provide repair, maintenance and installation of climate friendly bus shelters and to display advertising on the paper and digital shelter panels for a return of profit share.
      
      This will initially be in the Boroughs of Gosport , Hart and Rushmoor with scope for further areas to be encompassed into this contract.
      The remaining 8 Borough Councils in the Hampshire County council area can fall in scope for this contract , however there is no guarantee that they will do so . The numbers and locations of the shelters can change throughout the term of the contract and there is no guarantee of additional shelters being included in this tender. The estimation of value for the three localities is £35,334,000.00 over the 15 year term based on Authority spend on advertising. Further details can be found in the procurement documents.
      
      The shelters will be owned and maintained under the responsibility of the successful concessionaire. 
      
      The Contract will commence on 18th July 2024 and will be for a period of ten years with the option to extend for a further five years.
      
      Interested parties should register their interest in the project via the In-Tend website https://in-tendhost.co.uk/hampshire, and complete and submit the tender return document together with any supporting information requested by 14.00 hrs on Tuesday the 28th May 2024.  
      
      How to obtain the Tender Documents
      The Tender documents can be accessed when logged into In-Tend by selecting 'Tenders' then 'Current Tenders' and 'View Details' on the relevant tender advert and clicking the 'Express Interest' tab. Once in the tender there are five tabs - 'Tender', 'ITT - documents', 'Correspondence', 'Clarifications' and 'History'. Select the 2nd tab (ITT - documents) where you will find useful information under 'Tender Details' continue to scroll down to the heading 'Tender Documents Received' where you will be able to view / download the documents.

title: Targeted Tier 2 Weight Management Service via Physical Activity (Women)
description:
A pilot, multi component weight loss intervention that utilises group/team sport/physical activity as a key component, enabling eligible adult women in Gosport and Rushmoor who are overweight or obese to be supported to lose a minimum of 5% of their weight and increase levels of physical activity after 12-14 weeks.

The service will support adult women in Hampshire who want to or need to lose weight, through partaking in a programme with a physical activity as a major component to maximise their health and well being.
